touches.text: Test tiers: commit, hourly, daily and weekly. Each tier runs only what it must, so a commit needs only its own proofs and the long runs wait for the long tiers; nothing runs just in case.

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
The test before raising one: can only CC or Akien fix this? If not, it is a log line, not a trouble. One problem, one trouble.
Trouble: it has to be able to report when nothing else can, so a direct line makes sense for recovery (6.3.4).
Trouble tickets (3.4.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.3.7.1.3).
A diagnostic report, EXACTLY like the Trouble Tickets in the Number Five Crossbar Telephone Switch. It MUST include EVERYTHING needed to diagnose, isolate, and repair the trouble.
A second observation of an open trouble NEVER issues a new ticket; it increments a counter on the open one.

A trouble ticket is a work order. Whoever fixed it reports the fix to the originator (the device or machine that raised it), and the originator marks it fixed. A trouble that comes back is not designed for yet; if recurrent problems appear, we'll explore that.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
Transient: things held for seconds to days (mail, logs, test runs, trouble tickets, inference tickets). The logging tree.

Transient things may help debugging out to 30 days and won't be needed past that, eg an inference ticket looked at a week later because a bug turned up. No trouble should stand unresolved at 30 days; sleep's cleanup may be made to spare one that does.

A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
conflicts.ticket_says: When a door (cast or sorted) refuses to write a red's ticket, raise an unticketed trouble naming the door and the lacks, then re-raise the exception so the run exits non-zero. The red receives its ticket in a later run when the door succeeds, or when the proof reads green.
conflicts.why: Outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 requires 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds'. The ticket's work, when built as written, does not write a ticket for that red in that run—it writes a trouble instead. The constraint acknowledges this: 'the trouble never stands in for the ticket outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 requires...the red still needs its ticket'. This is a workaround (trouble as temporary record) for a case the outline does not account for, and the ticket itself states 'A door refusing a red's ticket is a defect against outline 9.4.2.3.7.5', not an exception the outline permits.
